summary: Juan Mendoza International Airport serves the city of Oruro in the Bolivian Altiplano, located at an elevation of approximately 3,700 meters above sea level, making it one of the higher airports in South America. The airport provides an important gateway to Oruro, a city famous for its rich mining heritage and the vibrant Carnaval de Oruro, a UNESCO-recognized cultural festival. It primarily handles domestic flights connecting Oruro with other Bolivian cities such as La Paz and Cochabamba.
faqs:
Q: What is the elevation of Juan Mendoza International Airport?
A: The airport sits at approximately 3,700 meters (12,140 feet) above sea level on the Bolivian Altiplano, which can affect passengers unaccustomed to high altitudes.

Q: Does Juan Mendoza International Airport offer international flights?
A: The airport primarily handles domestic flights within Bolivia. International travelers typically connect through El Alto International Airport in La Paz or Viru Viru International Airport in Santa Cruz.

Q: What is the best time to visit Oruro through this airport?
A: Late February to early March is ideal if you want to experience the famous Carnaval de Oruro, but flights and accommodations book up quickly during this period.

Q: Are there ATMs and currency exchange services at the airport?
A: Facilities at the airport are limited; it is advisable to exchange currency or withdraw Bolivianos in Oruro city center before traveling onward.
transport_tips: Taxis are the most common way to reach the airport, located about 4 kilometers from Oruro's city center, with a typical journey taking around 15 minutes. Pre-arranging transport through your hotel is recommended, especially during the busy Carnaval season when demand surges. Shared minibuses (micros) also serve the airport route but operate on less predictable schedules.
local_tip: Due to the high altitude, take it easy on arrival and stay well hydrated to avoid altitude sickness (soroche) before exploring Oruro, which sits at nearly 3,700 meters above sea level.
